questionText:
Consider the following two statements about regular languages:

$S_1$: Every infinite regular language contains an undecidable language as a subset.
$S_2$: Every finite language is regular.

Which one of the following choices is correct?
explanation:
Statement $S_1$: Every infinite regular language $L$ has $2^{\aleph_0}$ (uncountably many) subsets. Since the set of all decidable languages is countably infinite, uncountably many subsets of $L$ must be undecidable. Therefore, $S_1$ is true.

Statement $S_2$: Any finite language consists of a finite number of strings. Since a single string forms a regular language and regular languages are closed under finite union, every finite language is regular. Therefore, $S_2$ is true.

Hence, both $S_1$ and $S_2$ are true.
